bottleneck: AI can now design novel proteins, but most designs fail when expressed: misfolding, aggregation, poor solubility, and immunogenicity in humans kill candidates that looked perfect in silico. The gap between predicted structure and manufacturable, safe, functional therapeutic protein remains wide, because design models optimize for static structure while ignoring expression, stability, and immune visibility. Each failure costs months of wet-lab iteration, and the feedback loop from failure to better design is slow.
current_state: Designed enzymes and binders reach the clinic in a few cases, but the hit rate from computation to working therapeutic is still low. Experimental validation remains the bottleneck, not design generation.
title: De novo protein designs fail in expression
why_it_blocks: Protein design promises custom medicines on demand, but computation without reliable translation to working molecules is just expensive hypothesis generation. Closing the expression gap would industrialize the entire field.
